label: H.R. 6610

latest_action.text: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 40 - 2.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Pharmacists Fight Back in Federal Employee Health Benefit Plans Act sets rules for pharmacy benefit managers operating within Federal employee health benefit plans. It regulates pharmacy reimbursement rates, mandates the passing of manufacturer rebates directly to consumers at the point of sale and to health plans, prohibits specific network restrictions and practices favoring affiliated pharmacies, and establishes monetary penalties and debarment procedures for noncompliance enforced by the Office of Personnel Management.

affected_groups.effect: Receive prescription drug benefits under plans that must pass manufacturer rebates directly to them at the point of sale to lower out-of-pocket costs, and cannot be forced to use specific affiliated pharmacies.

Protected by standardized reimbursement rules for ingredient costs and professional dispensing fees, and shielded from post-adjudication fee reductions or network exclusions by pharmacy benefit managers.
Subject to strict operational restrictions regarding pharmacy networks, pricing, and affiliate preferences, and face monetary fines and potential debarment for violations.

Must ensure participating pharmacy benefit managers comply with new requirements, cooperate with Office of Personnel Management inspections, develop remediation plans if penalties accumulate, and face potential fines.

key_provisions: Requires pharmacy benefit managers to reimburse in-network pharmacies for ingredient costs based on the national average drug acquisition cost (or wholesale acquisition cost) plus up to 4 percent or $50, whichever is less.
Requires payment of a professional dispensing fee equal to the fee paid by the state under Title XIX of the Social Security Act.
Mandates that manufacturer rebates are applied at the point of sale to reduce patient copayments or coinsurance based on net cost, with the remainder remitted to the health plan carrier.
Prohibits pharmacy benefit managers from forcing patients to use specific or affiliated pharmacies, or restricting in-network pharmacies via certain accreditation, supply, or delivery limits.
Bans post-adjudication claim adjustments or fee reductions that lower pharmacy reimbursement.
Establishes civil monetary penalties of $10,000 per violation for pharmacy benefit managers and carriers, capped within specific 10-year limits.
Mandates the debarment of pharmacy benefit managers from administering benefits if they accumulate 10 or more civil monetary penalties within a 10-year period.
missing_information: The total financial impact on the Federal Employees Health Benefits Fund or federal budget is not provided.
The exact number of Federal employees and beneficiaries who will be directly affected is not stated.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Pharmacists Fight Back in Federal Employee Health Benefit Plans Act sets rules for pharmacy benefit managers operating within Federal employee health benefit plans. It regulates pharmacy reimbursement rates, mandates the passing of manufacturer rebates directly to consumers at the point of sale and to health plans, prohibits specific network restrictions and practices favoring affiliated pharmacies, and establishes monetary penalties and debarment procedures for noncompliance enforced by the Office of Personnel Management.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation alters how pharmacy benefit managers operate within the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program by imposing federal standards on pharmacy reimbursement, banning certain steering and fee practices, requiring rebate transparency at the point of sale, and establishing enforcement mechanisms through fines and debarment.
